title: Supervisory Findings and Remediation: From Risk Assessment to Closure
summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors reach findings and how licensees can respond with remediation that fixes root causes and closes issues on evidence.
intro: This training programme equips licensees to understand how supervisors reach and challenge their conclusions, and to respond to risk ratings, risk mitigation programmes and thematic reviews with remediation that works and evidence that closes issues.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To help boards, senior managers and control functions understand the path from a supervisory risk assessment to ratings, findings and required actions, and to manage remediation so that issues are fixed at their root and closed on evidence. Participants leave able to engage constructively with findings, design remediation that addresses underlying causes and respond well to thematic reviews.
sections.What It Covers: How supervisory conclusions are reached and challenged, risk ratings and engagement, risk mitigation programmes, choosing and planning remediation, evidencing closure, escalation and enforcement risk, and thematic reviews and industry reports.
Intended Audience: Board members and senior managers accountable for responding to supervisory findings
Compliance, risk and internal audit staff who coordinate remediation and track actions
Project and change managers who deliver remediation programmes
Learning Objectives: Explain how supervisors form, test and challenge their conclusions before findings are issued
Interpret risk ratings and what they mean for the firm's supervisory engagement
Analyse supervisory findings to identify incidents, control failures and underlying causes
Design remediation actions that define the outcome and can be evidenced
Manage remediation to closure and avoid escalation
Respond effectively to thematic reviews and industry findings
sections.Structure and Format: Six modules of about one hour each, delivered as a one-day workshop in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, built around a running case study. It can be delivered on its own or with the companion workshops on business models and on governance and supervisory interviews.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of supervisory engagement or remediation work is helpful. No prior training is required.
Core Reading: IMF, Good Supervision: Lessons from the Field (Working Paper WP/23/181, 2023)
FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
IOSCO, Objectives and Principles of Securities Regulation (2017)

modules.title: How Supervisors Reach Their Conclusions
modules.summary: How supervisory teams turn analysis into ratings and proposed actions, and how internal challenge and governance processes test their conclusions before findings reach the firm.
objectives: Describe how supervisors move from evidence to judgement
Explain the role of internal challenge in supervisory decisions
Anticipate what a well-reasoned finding looks like
syllabus: From desk review and visits to key vulnerabilities
Written rationales and the supervisory audit trail
Internal challenge and peer review of supervisory conclusions
Consistency across firms and over time

modules.title: Risk Ratings and Supervisory Engagement
modules.summary: What impact and risk ratings mean, how they drive the intensity of supervision and what the firm can do to understand and influence its risk profile.
objectives: Explain how ratings shape supervisory engagement
Identify the drivers of the firm's risk profile
syllabus: Impact, risk and the intensity of supervision
How ratings are communicated to the firm
Correcting factual errors and providing context
Improving the risk profile over time

modules.title: Risk Mitigation Programmes and Required Actions
modules.summary: How supervisors structure issues and actions, the range of tools from firm-led actions to formal measures, and how the escalation ladder works.
objectives: Read a supervisory issue and its required actions
Explain the range of supervisory tools and escalation
Recognise when a matter risks referral to enforcement
syllabus: Anatomy of a required action: issue, action, owner, date
Tools that work through the firm and formal supervisory measures
The escalation ladder and what triggers it
When findings become enforcement referrals

modules.title: Designing Remediation That Works
modules.summary: How to diagnose root causes and design remediation that defines the destination, has clear ownership and fixes the underlying control failure rather than the symptom.
objectives: Separate incident, control failure and underlying cause
syllabus: Incident, control failure and underlying cause
Define the destination, not the journey
Ownership, resourcing and realistic timelines
Case study: drafting the remediation plan

modules.title: Evidencing Closure and Avoiding Escalation
modules.summary: What evidence supervisors need before closing an action, how to report progress and how to handle slippage without losing credibility.
objectives: Assemble evidence that an action is complete and effective
Report remediation progress to the board and supervisor
Manage slippage and changes to agreed actions
syllabus: Completion versus effectiveness: testing the fix
Assurance from the second and third lines
Progress reporting and early warning of slippage
Case study: six months on

modules.title: Thematic Reviews and Industry Findings
modules.summary: How supervisors run thematic reviews, what they mean for firms in and outside the sample, and how to use published findings to strengthen the firm's own controls.
objectives: Explain how thematic reviews are scoped and run
Respond effectively when selected for a thematic review
Apply published thematic findings to the firm
syllabus: Why supervisors run thematic reviews
Responding to questionnaires, visits and feedback
Reading industry reports: complying with intent, not just wording
Workshop: a gap analysis against a thematic report

related.title: Engaging Effectively with Your Supervisor: How Firms Are Assessed
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how supervisors assess business models, governance and risk, so they can see themselves as the supervisor does and engage with confidence.

related.title: Fit and Proper for Firms: Appointing and Assessing Key Function Holders
related.summary: A nine-module programme showing firms how to appoint and assess key function holders, prepare applications and interviews, and manage fitness and certification on an ongoing basis.

related.title: Governance Reviews and Supervisory Interviews: Preparing Your Board and Management
related.summary: A one-day workshop on how supervisors assess governance and interview directors and staff, and how licensees can evidence effective governance and prepare openly.

related.title: Recovery and Wind-Down Planning for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms build credible recovery and wind-down plans, from scenarios and triggers to client asset return, testing and supervisory review.

related.title: Regulatory Investigations and Enforcement: Responding as a Firm
related.summary: A ten-module programme showing firms how to prepare for, manage and respond to supervisory investigations and enforcement, from first information request to settlement.

related.title: Regulatory Readiness: Authorisation and Supervisory Engagement
related.summary: A ten-module programme taking firms from licence application through to established supervision, showing how authorities assess applications and supervise new firms.
